They stand distinct from the **Devas**, who comprise all non-Mankind entities and celestial beings in the universe whose ancestral origins lie entirely outside the line of Manu.                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **The Ārya: The Faithful Bearers of the Lineage**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| While all sub-races of *manuṣya* share this divine origin through Manu, not all beings honor or maintain it. The *Ṛgveda* establishes a fundamental internal division within the race of man based on fidelity to this ancestral source. The **Ārya**---a word sharing its precise verbal root (ṛ), \"to move toward, to strive upward\") with **Ṛta**---designates those who actively move toward, embody, and preserve their divine source.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The Rigvedic poets explicitly define the Ārya by their living alignment with Ṛta. In *Ṛgveda* 1.51.8, the seer invokes the divine power to draw a clear distinction between those who uphold this divine lineage and those who have fallen away from it: *vijānīhy āryān ye ca dasyavo barhiṣmate randhayā śāsad avratān \|*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| \"Distinguish between the **Āryas** and those who are Dasyus; bring into subjection those who are without sacred vows (*avrata*)\...\" (*Ṛgveda* 1.51.8)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Here, the distinction is entirely spiritual, moral, and ancestral. The Dasyu or Anārya is described as *avrata* (without vows), *ayajyu* (non-sacrificing/unaligned), and *mṛdhravāc* (hostile or deceitful in speech). They are members of Mankind who have severed their connection to Ṛta through ignorance, delusion, and lawlessness. Conversely, the Ārya are designated in *Ṛgveda* 10.63.1 as the true sons of the solar source who are nourished directly by Ṛta: *yebhyo mātā madhumat pinvate divaḥ\...*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| \"Those for whom the mother yields sweet abundance\... those who are born of the Sun (*Sūrya*) and nourished by **Ṛta**.\" (*Ṛgveda* 10.63.1)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| To be an Ārya in the Rigvedic sense is to be a *ṛtāvān*---a possessor and practitioner of Ṛta---living with the dignity, truthfulness (*satya*), and moral strength appropriate to an heir of the Sun God.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **The Continuity of the Lineage: From Rigveda to the Solar Dynasties**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| This Rigvedic understanding of Ṛta as the divine source of man and Ārya as its noble keeper laid the foundation for the royal solar lineages (*Sūryavaṁśa*) preserved throughout the epics and early texts. The direct bloodline flowing from Vivasvān to Manu descended through King Ikṣvāku (Pāḷi: *Okkāka, Gautama lineage*), establishing an earthly lineage tasked with preserving Ṛta.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| When Lord Kṛṣṇa scolds Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukṣetra, calling his sudden collapse into despair **anārya-juṣṭam** (*Bhagavad Gītā* 2.2)---*\"unworthy of an Ārya\"*---he is directly invoking this Rigvedic inheritance. Kṛṣṇa admonishes Arjuna that yielding to weakness is a betrayal of his solar lineage, a denial of his origin in Ṛta, and behavior beneath the dignity of the race of man.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Similarly, this lineage reaches its ultimate spiritual fulfillment in the historical Buddha, Siddhartha of the Gautama lineage. Born of the Sākya clan---a direct branch of the Ikṣvāku solar line---the Buddha is repeatedly addressed in the earliest Pāḷi Canon as **Ādiccabandhu** (*\"Kinsman of the Sun God* **Ādicca***\"*). When the Buddha purified his mind (*citta*) of all worldly defilements (*rāga, dosa, moha*), he uncovered what he explicitly termed the **ancient path** (*purāṇaṁ maggaṁ*) to the ultimate liberation (*moksha*).                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| By practicing *Brahmacariya*---aligning fully with the purest Brahma standard---he brought the primordial, divine essence of Ṛta to its absolute perfection on Earth. He demonstrated how a noble being (*Ariya-puggala*) within Mankind can rise through Concentration (*Samādhi*) to the *Rūpa* realm as the final threshold, exit this universe of cause and effect, and escape involuntary reincarnation (*saṁsāra*) into the deathless realm (**Dhātu**) of **Nibbāna**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Svarga (heaven): The Celestial Abode of Solar Light**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Svarga** (स्वर्ग---literally \"the realm of light\" or \"attainment of the sun\"). Within the ontological framework of *Ṛta* (the divine essence) and the cosmic lineage of mankind (*manuṣya*), Svarga stands as a real, luminous, high-frequency celestial dimension, the *Rūpa* realm (*Rūpa-loka*) of the universe. It is the exalted realm where the fruits of living as an **Ārya**---one who actively maintains alignment with *Ṛta*---are fully realized in the presence of the solar deities and where ultimate liberation or release from this universe is achieved.                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **The Nature of Svarga: The Realm of Solar Light**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| In the Rigvedic cosmological architecture, the universe is structured into distinct tiers (*triloka*): the coarse physical earth (*Bhūmi*), the intermediate atmospheric realm (*Antarikṣa*), and the highest realm of light (*Svar* or *Svarga*). Svarga is characterized above all by pure light (*jyotiṣ*), completely free from the darkness, disease, and decay of the lower physical worlds.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The *Ṛgveda* portrays Svarga as the domain presided over by **Indra**, **Varuṇa**, and the **Ādityas**---the solar deities spawned directly from *Ṛta*. In *Ṛgveda* 9.113.7--9, the seer Rishi Kaśyapa explicitly describes Svarga as an immortal, imperishable realm of eternal radiance where the primordial divine essence flows without obstruction: *yatra jyotir ajasraṁ yasmin loke svar hitam \| tasmin māṁ dhehi pavamānāmṛte loke akṣite\...*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| \"Where light is everlasting, in the realm where the sun is placed---in that immortal, imperishable world, O Soma, place me\...\" (*Ṛgveda* 9.113.7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| *yatra rājā vaivasvato yatrāvarodhanaṁ divaḥ \| yatrāmūr mahatīr āpas tatra mām amṛtaṁ kṛdhī\...*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| \"Where Vaivasvata Manu\'s kingly father \[Vivasvān\] rules, where the secret realm of heaven lies, where the mighty waters flow---there make me immortal\...\" (*Ṛgveda* 9.113.8)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| In this celestial sphere, beings do not possess gross, meat-and-bone bodies bound to earthly gravity. Instead, those who enter Svarga are endowed with subtle, radiant forms (*divya-śarīra*) suited for a world where every sensory experience is an expression of divine abundance and harmony.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Svarga and the Destiny of the Ārya: The Path of the Fathers**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| For the earthly sub-race of mankind (*manuṣya*), Svarga represents the celestial reward attainable through high moral standard (*Sīla*), sacred vows (*vrata*), and sacral action in harmony with *Ṛta*. When an Ārya dies after fulfilling their duty, their mind (*citta*) and refined subtle form travel along the **Pitṛyāna** (the Path of the Ancestors) to join **Yama**---the first of mankind to conquer death and pave the trail to the solar heights.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| In *Ṛgveda* 10.14.7, the departed noble soul is instructed to leave behind all physical infirmity and ascend directly to the luminous assembly of the ancestors: *pretāhi pretāhi pathibhiḥ pūrvyair yatrā naḥ pūrve pitaraḥ pareyuḥ \| ubhā rājānā svadhayā madantā yamam paśyāsi varuṇaṁ ca devam \|\|* \"Go forth, go forth by those ancient paths along which our ancient fathers passed. You shall behold both King Yama and Varuṇa the God, rejoicing in their sacred feast.\" (*Ṛgveda* 10.14.7)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Svarga is thus the reunion grounds of the ancestral seed of Manu. It is where the pure spark of *manas* (mind), elevated through a lifetime of virtue, reunites with its solar origins in the upper heavens.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Svarga vs. Nibbāna-Dhātu: The Bound vs. The Unconditioned**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| While Svarga is a place of immense splendor, the ancient literature maintains a rigorous distinction between **Svarga** and **ultimate liberation** (*Nibbāna-Dhātu*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| NIBBĀNA-DHĀTU (Deathless, Beyond All Universes)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| - \[Exit\]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| PURE ABODES / BRAHMA REALMS                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| │                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| SVARGA (Heaven) (Luminous solar realm)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| - \[Virtue / Puṇya / Sīla\]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| EARTHLY HUMANS (Manuṣya)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Svarga is Within the World (*Loka*):** Because Svarga is a celestial realm within the universe, it remains governed by the fundamental laws of cause and effect. The life spans in Svarga are vast---spanning ages---yet they are finite. Once the accumulated power of one\'s righteous merit (*puṇya*) is eventually exhausted, the soul remains bound to the wheel of rebirth (*saṁsāra*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Nibbāna-Dhātu is Beyond the Universe:** In contrast, the ultimate goal uncovered by the ancient path (*purāṇaṁ maggaṁ*) of Gautama Buddha is not mere residence in a high heavenly world, but absolute transcendence.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Through the complete eradication of worldly defilements (*rāga, dosa, moha*), the noble practitioner (*Ariya-puggala*) uses the higher mental standard of Concentration (*Samādhi*)---specifically utilizing the **pure abode heaven** as the final gateway---to step outside the universe entirely, realizing permanent liberation in **Nibbāna-Dhātu**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| **Conclusion**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| In sum, the Rigvedic **Svarga** is the supreme celestial resting place for the noble heirs of Manu---a solar realm of pure light, vitality, and divine reward earned by living in accord with *Ṛta*. It serves as an essential staging ground in the cosmic architecture of mankind. Yet, for the fully awakened mind seeking absolute freedom from all conditioned worlds, Svarga is merely a lofty stepping stone on the ancient path of liberation (vimutti) toward the unconditioned, deathless realm beyond the cosmos.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

**\**

**2.[3](javascript:void(0))   klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha, naitat tvayy upapadyate;**

**        kṣudraṁ hṛdaya-daurbalyaṁ, tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa.**

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Do not yield to unmanliness (weakness, faint-heartedness), O Pārtha (Arjuna, son of Pṛthā); it is not fitting for you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and arise, O scorcher of foes!\"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Commentary**: Within the framework of **Ṛta** (the divine source) and the cosmic lineage of **Mankind** (*manuṣya*), Kṛṣṇa\'s command carries deep ancestral and spiritual weight:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **A Betrayal of the Noble Lineage:** Kṛṣṇa addresses Arjuna as **Pārtha** and **Parantapa** (\"scorcher of foes\") to remind him of who he is. For an Ārya descended from the solar line (*Sūryavaṁśa*), slipping into *klaibyam* (impotence/unmanliness) is a degradation of the pure seed of man (*manas*). It is an act of stepping down from the dignity of *Ṛta* into lower, chaotic, animalistic reactivity.                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **The Nature of *Hṛdaya-daurbalyam* (Heart-Weakness):** Arjuna's grief was disguised as compassion, but Kṛṣṇa exposes it for what it truly is: **kṣudra**---petty, localized emotion born of delusion (*moha*). True spiritual compassion (*karuṇā*) comes from high mental strength and clarity (*Samādhi*); emotional collapse on the battlefield is merely a failure of the heart to maintain its noble alignment.                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **The Call to Arise (*Uttiṣṭha*):** *\"Arise!\"* is not merely an order to pick up a physical bow. It is the universal call to all mind-endowed sub-races of Mankind to **strive upward** (the core root of Ārya: ṛ, \"to move toward, to rise\"). Kṛṣṇa demands that Arjuna align his *citta* (mind) with the unyielding standard of the Ārya, discard the temporary weakness of the physical form, and execute his sacred duty in accord with cosmic law. |


***\***

***Arjuna uvāca***

**2.[4](javascript:void(0))   kathaṁ bhīṣmam ahaṁ saṇkhye, droṇaṁ ca madhusūdana;**

**        iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi, pūjārhāv ari-sūdana.**

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Arjuna said: O Madhusūdana (Kṛṣṇa, slayer of the demon Madhu), how can I strike back with arrows in battle against Bhīṣma and Droṇa---two men who are worthy (*arha*) of my highest reverence (*pūjā* = worship/honor), O slayer of enemies?\"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Commentary**: Arjuna's response to Kṛṣṇa highlights the deep conflict between **localized human attachment** and the **uncompromising cosmic law of Ṛta**:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **The Conflict of Respect vs. Cosmic Duty (*Dharma*):** Arjuna points out that Bhīṣma and Droṇa are not ordinary adversaries; they are his elders, elders who embodied the sacred traditions of his lineage. In traditional society, striking elders (*pūjārhau*---those worthy of worship) breaks social harmony. Arjuna argues that attacking them would be a violation of *Sīla* (virtuous conduct).                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **The Epithets of Kṛṣṇa (*Madhusūdana* & *Arisūdana*):** By addressing Kṛṣṇa as *Arisūdana* (\"slayer of enemies\") and *Madhusūdana* (\"slayer of the demon Madhu\"), Arjuna uses subtle irony. He is saying: *\"You are accustomed to destroying actual enemies and demons, Kṛṣṇa---but these men are not my enemies; they are my venerated teachers and elders.\"*                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **The Delusion (*Moha*) of Emotional Ties:** While Arjuna\'s argument appears noble on the surface, Kṛṣṇa will go on to reveal that Arjuna is caught in worldly delusion. Bhīṣma and Droṇa, despite their personal stature, have aligned themselves with the unrighteous forces of Duryodhana, thereby severing their alignment with **Ṛta**. Arjuna\'s reluctance to strike them is not true spiritual wisdom, but an emotional attachment to physical bodies and worldly roles, blinding him to his higher duty as an **Ārya** to uphold divine order above personal sentiment. |


**2.[5](javascript:void(0))   gurūn ahatvā hi mahānubhāvān, śreyo bhoktuṁ bhaikṣyam apīha loke; hatvārtha-kāmāṁs tu gurūn ihaiva, bhuñjīya bhogān rudhira-pradigdhān.**

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| It is surely better to live in this world even on begged alms than to slay these noble, great-souled teachers. For if I kill these gurus---even if they are bound to worldly wealth and desire---all the pleasures I enjoy here in this world would be smeared with their blood!\"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Commentary**: This verse reveals the exact nature of Arjuna\'s internal crisis and why Kṛṣṇa calls it a delusion:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **The Misapplication of Renunciation (*Bhaikṣyam, Pāḷi: bhikkhā or bhikkhācāra*):** Arjuna proposes living off alms (*bhaikṣyam*), mimicking the lifestyle of a *samaṇa* or **brahmana**. However, he is choosing this not out of genuine disenchantment with the world, but out of fear of committed action and emotional aversion to killing his kin. He mistakes passive withdrawal for true spiritual nobility.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **The Trait of *Artha-Kāmān* (Bound to Wealth and Desire):** Arjuna acknowledges a difficult truth about his gurus: Bhīṣma and Droṇa, despite their greatness (*mahānubhāvān*), are fighting on the side of unrighteousness (*Adharma*) because they are bound by obligation to the royal wealth and throne of Duryodhana (*artha-kāmān*). Yet Arjuna\'s personal attachment makes him hesitate to enforce divine law against them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Blood-Stained Enjoyment (*Rudhirapradigdha*):** Arjuna perceives victory as bringing only worldly enjoyment (*bhogān*). He fears that winning kingdom and sovereignty through the death of his elders will poison his mind with guilt. He remains trapped in the worldly framework of cause and effect, unable to see the war through Kṛṣṇa\'s lens---as an unyielding divine realignment necessary to purge unrighteousness and restore **Ṛta**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **pravrajyā** (Pāḷi: *pabbajjā*) and **bhaikṣyam** (Pāḷi: *bhikkhā* or *bhikkhācāra*)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Both represent two distinct phases along the ancient path: **pabbajjā** is the radical, ontological transition out of worldly household life, while **bhaikṣyam** is the daily, physical discipline of living on alms that sustains one who has departed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Pabbajjā (*पब्बज्जा* / Sanskrit: *Pravrajyā*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Etymology:** Derived from pa- (forth, away), vraj (to go, to walk).
