| **Tūṣṇīṁ Babhūva (\"He Became Silent\"):** By falling silent immediately after his declaration, Arjuna exhausts his own arguments and rationalizations. This self-imposed silence (*tūṣṇīm*) signifies the end of his personal ego-driven deliberations and creates the essential space needed to transition from a confused warrior into a receptive student (*śiṣya*), paving the way for Kṛṣṇa's teachings to begin.                                                                                                          |


**\**

**2.[10](javascript:void(0))   tam uvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ, prahasann iva bhārata;**

**        senayor ubhayor madhye, viṣīdantam idam vacaḥ.**

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| To him who was despairing in the midst of the two armies, O Bhārata (Dhṛtarāṣṭra), Hṛṣīkeśa, smiling as it were, spoke these words. |
+=====================================================================================================================================+

***Śrī-Bhagavān uvāca***

**2.[11](javascript:void(0))   aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṁ, prajñā-vādāṁś ca bhāṣase;**

**        gatāsūn agatāsūṁś ca, nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ.**

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Then Bhagava Kṛṣṇa said: You grieve for those who need not be grieved for, yet you speak words of pseudo-wisdom. The truly wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Commentary**: This verse marks the exact point where Kṛṣṇa cuts through Arjuna's intellectual posturing. Kṛṣṇa\'s opening statement becomes a direct critique of **pseudo-wisdom (*prajñā-vāda*)**:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Exposing pseudo-wisdom (*Prajñā-vādāṁś Ca Bhāṣase*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| In Chapter 1, Arjuna delivered high-sounding speeches about duty, lineage, and social decay. Kṛṣṇa dismisses these arguments as *prajñā-vāda*---mere words of intellectual pretension. Arjuna talks like a liberated sage, yet he is paralyzed by grief, *rāga* (attachment), and *moha* (delusion). Kṛṣṇa points out the fatal flaw: **if your \"wisdom\" leaves you weeping and attached to the worldly frame, it is not wisdom at all.**                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **The True *Paṇḍita* Discerns *Anicca***                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| A true *paṇḍita* (one possessed of genuine discernment) does not mourn the living (*agatāsu*) or the dead (*gatāsu*) which the concept of bodily death is all about. This is not because the body is an \"illusion\" that doesn\'t exist, but because all physical and mental phenomena belong to this world (*loka*). They are subject to cause, effect, decay, and death (*dukkha*). Mourning physical bodies that rise and fall reveals a fundamental delusion: **clinging (*upādāna*) to phenomena that are not our true self (Ātman), nor part of our true self (Ātman), nor belonging to our true self (Ātman).** |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **The Call to Disenchantment**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Grief stems directly from the failure to see that all worldly *dhamma* are impermanent. Kṛṣṇa\'s opening line is an immediate call to cultivate *nibbidā* (disenchantment from the worldly). To stop mourning the living or the dead, one must cease identifying with the mortal frame, abandon *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, and begin the practical work of *Sīla*, *Samādhi*, and *Paññā* to transcend *saṃsāra* entirely.                                                                                                                                                                                             |


**2.[12](javascript:void(0))   na tv evāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ, na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ;**

**        na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ, sarve vayam ataḥ param.**

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Never indeed was there a time when I (aham) did not exist, nor you (tvam), nor these rulers of men (janādhipāḥ, lords and kings); nor will every one of us (sarve) cease to exist hereafter.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Commentary**: From the mechanical reality of *saṃsāra*, Kṛṣṇa is laying bare the **sobering diagnosis of our involuntary reincarnation**:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **1). Diagnosing Beginningless *Saṃsāra* (*Na Tv Evāhaṁ Jātu Nāsam\...*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Kṛṣṇa highlights an inescapable truth: our existence within this cosmic cycle did not begin on this battlefield, nor did it start with this current physical birth. Beings have been wandering through the continuous loop of death and rebirth through beginningless time (*anamatagga saṃsāra*).                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| As long as the root causes---*rāga* (worldly craving and attachment), *dosa* (fear and anger), and *moha* (ignorance and delusion)---remain uneradicated, the momentum of craving (*taṇhā*) forces continuous, unbroken continuity from one birth to the next.                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **2). The Reality of the Higher-Dimensional Ātman (*Na Tv Evāhaṁ Jātu Nāsam\...*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Kṛṣṇa is directly asserting the real, enduring existence of the inner entity---the Ātman. It is not an illusion or a temporary bundle of physical processes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Because the Ātman is a higher-dimensional structure, its existence spans far beyond a single 3D physical lifespan. Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, and all these lords and kings have existed as real entities through long spans of time. They do not pop into existence at physical birth, nor are they erased at physical death.                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| When the physical 3D body drops away on the battlefield, the Ātman does not cease to exist (*na eva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ*). It survives physical death because physical weapons and physical forces cannot destroy a higher-dimensional entity. Surviving physical death, however, is **not** the same as absolute immortality.                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **3). The Prison of Involuntary Reincarnation in the Universe**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| The fact that all these beings continue to exist *ataḥ param* (hereafter) highlights the core danger of *saṃsāra*: **continuation within this universe without absolute safety**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| As long as the Ātman remains inside this universe, it is subject to universal law of decay or destruction. Simply surviving physical death to be reborn again in another physical frame is not freedom---it is an endless loop inside a universe where decay still applies.                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| To realize that we, along with these lords and kings (*janādhipāḥ*), have been endlessly recycled through different forms across aeons brings deep disenchantment (*nibbidā*). The only true resolution is not to celebrate endless rebirth, but to break the cycle by eradicating worldly craving and clinging entirely through the ancient path of liberation.                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Key Takeaway:**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| The Ātman is real and outlives the 3D body, but its survival within the universe is still relative. True, absolute, unconditioned deathlessness cannot be found anywhere inside this universe. It is realized only when the purified mind/Ātman cuts through *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, and uses the pure abode Brahma realms as the gateway to exit this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu,** the realm of Nibbāna. |


**2.[13](javascript:void(0))   dehino 'smin yathā dehe, kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā;**

**        tathā dehāntara-prāptir, dhīras tatra na muhyati.**

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Just as for the embodied (Dehin, *Ātman*) in this physical body there is childhood, youth, and old age, in the same way there is the acquisition of another physical body. The wise (dhīra) is not deluded by this.                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Commentary**: This makes a literal distinction between the **physical body (*deha*)** and the **embodied (*Dehin*, *Ātman*)** who occupies it.                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| The physical body undergoes continuous, visible changes: childhood, youth, and old age. The embodied (*Dehin*, *Ātman*) is the real, higher-dimensional entity inhabiting this physical body during its temporary lifespan.                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| When the physical body dies, the embodied (*Dehin*, *Ātman*) is not destroyed by physical decay or physical weapons.                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| The transition at physical death is literally *dehāntara-prāptiḥ*---the acquisition of another physical body. The higher-dimensional entity simply moves into another physical body.                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **The Clarity of the Wise (*Dhīras Tatra Na Muhyati*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| The wise (*dhīra*) does not get confused or deluded by physical death because they recognize two facts:                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Physical death does not erase the embodied (Dehin, Ātman)**, so grieving the loss of a physical body is unnecessary.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Moving from one physical body to another is still involuntary reincarnation.** Merely surviving physical death does not mean safety. As long as the embodied (Dehin, Ātman) remains in this universe, it is subject to cosmic law of decay and death.                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| The embodied (*Dehin*, *Ātman*) outlives the physical body, but repeatedly acquiring new physical bodies keeps one trapped in the universe. True freedom requires eradicating *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, using the pure abode Brahma realms as the gateway to exit this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**. |


**2.[14](javascript:void(0))   mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya, śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ;**

**        āgamāpāyino 'nityās, tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata.**

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Sensory contacts, O son of Kuntī (Arjuna), give rise to cold, heat, pleasure, and pain. They come and go and are impermanent; endure them, O descendant of Bharata.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Commentary**: **1). The Nature of Sensory Contact (*Mātrā-Sparśāḥ*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Kṛṣṇa points directly to the physical mechanism of experience: sensory contacts (*mātrā-sparśāḥ*). When the sensory faculties of the physical body meet external objects, they automatically generate sensations---cold, heat, pleasure, and *dukkha* (pain). These sensory impacts belong strictly to this world. They are *āgamāpāyinaḥ* (coming and going) and *anityāḥ* (impermanent). They rise, linger briefly, and fall away.                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **2). Severing the Reaction Chain**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Grief, paralysis, and worldly attachment arise when a person reacts to these temporary sensory contacts with *rāga* (craving and attachment) or *dosa* (fear and anger). Arjuna's hesitation on the battlefield is driven by his aversion to physical pain, grief, and the destruction of physical bodies. Kṛṣṇa instructs him to **endure them (*tāṁs titikṣasva*)**---not through passive submission, but by recognizing that these physical sensations do not define or destroy the embodied (Dehin, Ātman). |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **3). Enduring Sensory Flux as Spiritual Training**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Enduring sensory impacts without generating craving or aversion breaks the chain of compulsion. If one is constantly driven by physical pleasure and repelled by physical pain, the mind remains trapped in the low-dimensional currents of the universe.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| For the embodied (*Dehin*, *Ātman*), cultivating transcendental release (*upekkhā*) toward these impermanent sensory contacts is essential discipline. It prevents the generation of *kamma* and the accumulation of *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, establishing the Concentration (Samādhi) needed to ultimately exit this universe of decay through the gateway of the pure anode Brahma realms into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**.                                                                                          |


**2.[15](javascript:void(0))   yaṁ hi na vyathayanty ete, puruṣaṁ puruṣarṣabha;**

**        sama-duḥkha-sukhaṁ dhīraṁ, so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate.**

+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| O best among men (Arjuna), the person whom these sensory impacts do not agitate, who remains equal in pain and pleasure, that wise (dhīra) one becomes fit for the Deathless (**amṛtatvāya**).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **1). Immunity to Sensory Agitation (*Na Vyathayanti*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Following verse 2.14, Kṛṣṇa highlights the result of mastering sensory impacts. The sensory impacts (*ete*)---heat, cold, physical pain, and physical pleasure---ceaselessly hit the physical body. However, the person (*puruṣa*) who does not allow these contact points to agitate (*na vyathayanti*) their mind breaks the grip of worldly conditioning. When physical pain or pleasure no longer triggers *rāga* (craving) or *dosa* (anger), the mind stops creating new binding *kamma*.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **2). Equanimity of the Wise (*Sama-Duḥkha-Sukhaṁ Dhīram*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The wise (*dhīra*) maintains complete equanimity (*sama*) regardless of whether physical circumstances bring *duḥkha* (pain) or *sukha* (pleasure). This equanimity is not mere numbness; it is the deep, unwavering insight that physical pleasure and pain are transient occurrences belonging strictly to this world. They cannot touch, stain, or destroy the embodied (Dehin, Ātman) if treat them equanimous.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **3). Becoming Fit for the Deathless (*So 'mṛtatvāya Kalpate*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| By remaining unagitated, that practitioner becomes fit (*kalpate*) for *Amṛtatva*---the **Deathless**. Simply surviving physical death to acquire body after body inside this universe is **not** *Amṛtatva*; it is just the continuation of involuntary reincarnation which leads to eventual ultimate death. True *Amṛtatva* (the Deathless) is realized only when the mind is able to be released from the universe by being purified of *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*. This unwavering equanimity is what prepares the embodied (Dehin, Ātman) to navigate the final threshold to exit this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**, the ultimate and deathless realm of absolute peace and bliss. |


**2.[16](javascript:void(0))   nāsato vidyate bhāvo, nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ;**

**        ubhayor api dṛṣṭo 'ntas, tv anayos tattva-darśibhiḥ.**

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| There is no rise to become (bhāva) for the unreal (asat), nor is there cease to become (abhāva) for the real (sat). The ultimate truth of both of these has indeed been seen by the seers of reality/ truth (tattva-darśin).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **1). The Unreal Has No True \"Rise to Become\" (*Nāsato Vidyate Bhāvo*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The physical body, its sensory contacts (*mātrā-sparśāḥ*), and the resulting **sensory sensations** (cold, heat, physical pleasure, and *dukkha*/pain) are all *asat* (unreal). Because these physical structures and feelings are merely transient, conditioned manifestations governed by cause and effect, they possess no enduring, independent \"rise to become,\" \"to come into being\", or \"to manifest as a state or life form\" (*bhāva*) life form or stable reality. They constantly arise, fluctuate, decay, and fall away. They belong strictly to this world (*loka*) and can never offer a permanent identity that our mind can rest on. |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **2). The Real (Sat) Cannot \"Cease to Become\" Through Physical Death (*Nābhāvo Vidyate Sataḥ*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The real, higher-dimensional embodied (Dehin, Ātman) is *sat*. When the physical body dies and its sensory sensations cease, the *sat* does **not** undergo *abhāva*---it does not cease to become, nor is it annihilated. Physical weapons, physical decay, and the ending of 3D sensory inputs have zero power to destroy a higher-dimensional entity. However, because physical death cannot destroy or erase the real (*sat*), it provides no exit from the cycle.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **3). The Law of Kamma and Forced Reincarnation**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Because the real (*sat*) cannot undergo *abhāva* through physical death, the unresolved mental phenomena---the accumulated *kammic* momentum, craving (*taṇhā*), and aversion to sensory sensations (*dosa*)---remain fully intact. Under the unyielding law of cause and effect (*kamma*), this energetic drive **forces** the real (*sat*) into its next \"rise to become\" (*bhāva*) as a new life form within the universe. Dying physically and shedding physical sensory sensations does not bring peace; it simply triggers another involuntary, forced incarnation into another physical or subtle body.                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **4). The Discernment of the Seers of Reality (*Tattva-darśin*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The *tattva-darśins* (seers of reality/truth) see the complete truth of both dynamics: They do not grieve the destruction of the physical body or the cessation of its sensory sensations (*asat*), because those were never enduring life forms or permanent states to begin with. They realize that surviving physical death is not a victory---as long as the real (*sat*) remains trapped in the momentum of forced *bhava* inside this universe, it remains bound to cosmic law of decay and death, and leads to inevitable ultimate death.                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| The unreal physical body and its sensory sensations naturally dissolve, while the real (Dehin, Ātman) cannot be destroyed by physical death. But because it cannot cease to become through death, it is relentlessly forced into new life forms by the law of *kamma*. The only way to stop this involuntary reincarnation is to eradicate *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, using the pure abode Brahma realms as the gateway to exit this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**, where forced *bhava* ends forever.                                                                                                                                        |


**2.[17](javascript:void(0))   avināśi tu tad viddhi, yena sarvam idaṁ tatam;**

**        vināśam avyayasyāsya, na kaścit kartum arhati.**

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Know that to be imperishable (avināśi) by which all this is pervaded; no one is capable of causing the destruction of this indestructible (avyayasya, Dehin, Ātman). |
+======================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[18](javascript:void(0))   antavanta ime dehā, nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ;**

**        anāśino 'prameyasya, tasmād yudhyasva bhārata.**

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| These physical bodies of the continuously lasting (nitya), physically non-perishing (anāśin), and physically immeasurable (aprameya) embodied (Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman) are said to be finite (antavanta). Therefore, fight, O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Commentary: De-Mystifying the Three Qualities of the Embodied**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Traditional translations routinely inflate the terms ***nitya***, ***anāśin***, and ***aprameya*** into sweeping, abstract metaphysical dogma---rendering them as *\"eternal,\" \"indestructible,\"* and *\"immeasurable.\"* This vague language obscures the operational reality of the text. In the direct context of Arjuna's battlefield paralysis, Kṛṣṇa is pointing out a concrete dimensional boundary: **the real inner entity (Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman) simply operates beyond the physical plane and easily survives physical realm changes.** |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **1). *Nityasya* (*Nitya*): \"Eternal\" vs. \"Continuously Lasting\"**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Traditional Error:** Translating *nitya* as \"eternal\" smuggles in an unconditioned, timeless state, confusing the embodied entity inside *saṃsāra* with ultimate liberation (*Nibbāna*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Etymological Root:** Derived from the prefix **ni** (*\"downward,\" \"inward,\" \"dwelling within\"*) + the suffix **-tya** (*\"belonging to,\" \"abiding in\"*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Literal Sense:** *Ni-tya* literally means *\"inwardly abiding\"* or *\"that which stays continuously in its own state.\"*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **The Clarification:** Etymologically, *nitya* denotes **uninterrupted continuity across time**. It means the embodied entity stays inwardly present and continuously lasts through physical realm changes while the outer 3D physical body (*deha*) crumbles. It is \"eternally\" present only relative to the temporary physical vehicle, remaining bound to cosmic cycles until ultimate release.                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **2). *Anāśinaḥ*: Generic \"Indestructible\" vs. \"Physically Non-Perishing\"**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Traditional Error:** Translating *anāśin* as a blanket \"indestructible\" hides the specific physical threat Kṛṣṇa is addressing on the battlefield.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Etymological Root:** Privative prefix **a-** (*\"non-\" / \"not\"*) + **nāśin** (from the verbal root **naś**, *\"to disappear,\" \"to perish,\" \"to undergo physical destruction/dissolution\"*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Literal Sense:** *A-nāśin* means *\"non-disappearing\"* or *\"immune to physical ruin.\"*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **The Clarification:** In Chapter 2 (and explicitly reinforced in 2.17, 2.20, and 2.23), naś addresses Arjuna's fear that physical weapons (*śastrāṇi*), fire, or physical trauma can annihilate a life. *Anāśin* means the embodied entity is **physically non-perishing**---physical weapons operate strictly on a lower dimensional plane and cannot cause its dissolution or physical death.                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **3). *Aprameyasya*: Mystical \"Immeasurable\" vs. \"Physically Immeasurable\"**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Traditional Error:** Translating *aprameya* as \"immeasurable\" makes it sound like an incomprehensible theological mystery rather than a statement about physical metrics.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Etymological Root:** Prefix **a-** (*\"not\"*) + **pra-** (*\"forth/intensively\"*) + **meya** (future passive participle from **mā**, *\"to measure, gauge, weigh, or bound\"*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Literal Sense:** *A-prameya* means *\"incapable of being measured or bounded by empirical means (pramāṇa).\"*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
