|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **The Clarification:** A 3D physical body can be measured (*meya*) using length, mass, volume, or physical instruments. Because the embodied entity is a higher-dimensional structure, it cannot be detected, weighed, or bounded by physical tools or sensory organs. It is strictly **unmeasurable by physical means**.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| These three terms do not mean the embodied entity has achieved ultimate salvation. They simply define its dimensional immunity: physical weapons cannot kill it (*anāśin*), physical scales cannot weigh it (*aprameya*), and physical death cannot stop it from persisting (*nitya*). It easily survives physical realm changes---which is precisely why dying physically changes nothing, and why forced reincarnation (*bhava*) remains a constant trap until the roots of *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha* are destroyed.                                |


**2.[19](javascript:void(0))   ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ, yaś cainaṁ manyate hatam;**

**        ubhau tau na vijānīto, nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate.**

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| He who thinks this (Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman) is a killer, and he who thinks this is killed---both of them do not understand; this neither kills nor is killed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Commentary**: Kṛṣṇa addresses two mirror-image delusions that cripple the unminded practitioner: **The illusion of being the slayer:** Thinking that one\'s physical actions can slice, sever, or destroy the actual living entity (*hantāram*). **The illusion of being the slayed:** Thinking that one\'s real inner essence is annihilated when the 3D physical body is struck down (*hatam*). Those who hold either view lack true discernment (*na vijānītaḥ*). They conflate lower-dimensional physical interactions with the destruction of the higher-dimensional occupant. |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Physical Instruments Touch Only Physical Matter (*Nāyaṁ Hanti Na Hanyate*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The verb root **han** explicitly denotes physical slaying, trauma, or termination of physical life functions. The real embodied (Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman) does not perform physical slaying (*na hanti*), because physical weapons and physical movement operate strictly on the lower 3D plane of *asat*. Likewise, it is impossible for the real embodied entity to be physically slain (*na hanyate*). A blade cuts flesh and breaks bone; it cannot sever or destroy a higher-dimensional entity that merely pervades and animates the physical vehicle.                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **The Ethical and Kammic Illusion**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Arjuna's despair was built on the belief that fighting in the war would make him the ultimate destroyer of his relatives\' lives. Kṛṣṇa clarifies the mechanics: Physical death on the battlefield is simply the termination of the physical body (*deha*), which was already *antavantaḥ* (destined to end, as stated in 2.18). Striking a body does not erase the occupant. The real entity simply survives the physical realm change untouched by the blade.                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Note: The Danger of Misinterpreting \"Neither Kills Nor Is Killed\"**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **The Reincarnation Trap:** A common misunderstanding of 2.19 is to conclude that because the embodied entity cannot be killed (*na hanyate*), physical actions are completely consequence-free. This is a fatal error inside *saṃsāra*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| While physical weapons cannot slay the higher-dimensional entity (*Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman*), the **intent** and **volition** behind physical actions generate immediate *kammic* seeds. If an action is driven by *rāga* (craving and attachment) or *dosa* (fear, anger violence/ill-will), it binds the actor to the law of cause and effect.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| The entity cannot be destroyed by a sword, but it **can** be dragged into lower realms of severe *dukkha* by its own accumulated *kamma*. Physical death does not kill you---it simply forces your next involuntary \"rise to become\" (*bhāva*). True escape from this cycle is accomplished not by physical death, but by eradicating *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, using the pure abode Brahma realms as the gateway to transcend this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**.                                                                                                     |


**2.[20](javascript:void(0))   na jāyate mriyate vā kadācin, nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ;**

**ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṁ purāṇo, na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre.**

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| It is never born into physical existence (na **jāyate**), nor does it undergo physical death (**mriyate**); nor, having once manifested (**bhūtvā**), will it cease to manifest (**bhavitā**) again. Unborn (into physical existence) (**ajaḥ**), continuously lasting (**nitya**), unceasing (won't stop to manifest naturally unless by practicing the liberation path) (**śāśvata**), and ancient (**purāṇa**), it is not physically slain when the physical body (**śarīra**) is slain. |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **1). Immunity to Physical Birth and Physical Death (*Na Jāyate Mriyate Vā Kadācin*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Physical bodies (*śarīra*) are generated through physical assembly and destroyed through physical trauma or decay. Kṛṣṇa explicitly clarifies that the real embodied entity (*Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman*) operates completely outside this 3D cycle. It is never born into physical existence (*na jāyate*), nor does it undergo physical death (*mriyate*). Physical birth and physical death are merely events that happen to the outer physical vehicle (*asat*).                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **2). Perpetuated Manifestation Without Natural End (*Na Bhūtvā Bhavitā Vā Na Bhūyaḥ*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| When a physical body dies, the real entity does **not** cease to manifest (*bhavitā*). Having once manifested (*bhūtvā*), it does not stop manifestation naturally (*abhāva*) upon the breakdown of the physical vehicle. Because physical death cannot stop the underlying momentum of mental phenomena and *kammic* seeds, the process of manifestation (*bhava*) naturally continues to repeat itself across physical and subtle realms.                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **3). The Four Precise Attributes of the Embodied**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| - **Ajaḥ (Unborn into physical existence):** It is not created by physical causes, physical matter, or 3D biological reproduction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| - **Nityaḥ (Continuously lasting):** Inwardly abiding (*ni-tya*) across realm changes; it persists unbroken while outer physical bodies crumble.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| - **Śāśvataḥ (Unceasing):** Its cycle of manifestation will **not stop naturally** on its own, nor will physical death end it. It is an unceasing momentum that can *only* be stopped intentionally by practicing the ancient liberation path.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| - **Purāṇaḥ (Ancient):** Pre-exists the current physical body, having already persisted through countless prior incarnations and realm transitions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **4). Physical Destruction vs. Higher-Dimensional Continuance (*Na Hanyate Hanyamāne Śarīre*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| When the physical body (*śarīra*) is struck down, pierced by weapons, or destroyed on the battlefield, the embodied entity inside is **not physically slain (*na hanyate*)**. Physical blades and arrows operate strictly on the lower 3D plane. They terminate the physical functions of the coarse vehicle, while the higher-dimensional occupant simply survives the transition by physical weapons.                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Note: Why Unceasing Manifestation Is a Trap**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **The Reincarnation Mechanism:** Kṛṣṇa's description in 2.20 is often mistakenly read as a comforting statement of eternal safety. In reality, it outlines the exact mechanism of the *saṃsāric* trap.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Because the embodied entity is *śāśvata* (**unceasing---it will not stop manifesting naturally**), physical death offers zero escape or non-existence. When the physical body (*śarīra*) is slain, the real entity is forced into another \"rise to become/manifest\" (*bhāva*) driven by cause and effect, accumulated *kamma*, and unresolved craving (*taṇhā*).                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| It will continue to be reborn indefinitely until the chain is deliberately broken. Unceasing manifestation ends **only** through the complete eradication of *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, establishing Concentration (*Samādhi*) to pass through the gateway of the pure abode Brahma realms and exit this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**.                                                                                                                                         |


**2.[21](javascript:void(0))   vedāvināśinaṁ nityaṁ, ya enam ajam avyayam;**

**        kathaṁ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha, kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam.**

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| He who knows this (Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman) to be physically indestructible (avināśin), continuously lasting (nitya), unborn into physical existence (aja), and inexhaustible (avyaya)---how can that person, O Pārtha (Arjuna), cause anyone to be slain, or whom does he slay?\"                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **1). Direct Knowledge of Dimensional Immunity (*Vedāvināśinaṁ Nityam*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Kṛṣṇa shifts from describing the nature of the embodied entity to describing the **understanding of the person who knows it** (*veda*). The practitioner who directly discerns the true nature of the embodied (*Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman*) knows that it possesses four distinct attributes:                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| - **Avināśin:** Physically indestructible; physical weapons and lower-dimensional forces cannot dissolve it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| - **Nitya:** Continuously lasting; it inwardly abides (*ni-tya*) across physical realm transitions while outer physical vehicles crumble.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| - **Aja:** Unborn into physical existence; it is not produced by 3D physical causes or biological reproduction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| - **Avyaya:** inexhaustible; it does not undergo the physical breakdown, erosion, or age-related decay of *asat*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **2). The Illusion of Cause and Agency in Physical Slaying (*Kathaṁ Sa Puruṣaḥ\...*)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Kṛṣṇa asks two rhetorical questions: *\"How can that person cause anyone to be slain (ghātayati), or whom does he slay (hanti)?\"*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| When a person striking on the battlefield operates with true discernment, they realize that physical weapons act only upon *asat*---the coarse, 3D vehicle (*deha/śarīra*) which was already bound by physical laws to reach its natural end (*antavantaḥ*). A physical blade cannot sever, erase, or cause the destruction (*vināśa*) of the higher-dimensional occupant inside. Therefore, on a fundamental dimensional level, physical action cannot \"slay\" the real life of a living entity. |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Note: The Danger of Misinterpreting Non-Slaying**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **The Kammic Reality:** This verse is frequently misunderstood as a license to disregard physical harm or violence under the guise that \"nobody really dies.\" Such a view is a severe distortion of the Dhamma.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| While physical weapons touch only the physical body (*asat*) and cannot destroy the higher-dimensional entity (*Śarīrin, Dehin, Ātman*), **the mental volition driving physical actions generates direct kammic seeds**. Acting out of *dosa* (ill-will/hatred) or *rāga* (attachment/selfish craving) creates heavy, binding *kamma* regardless of whether the target\'s inner entity survives physical death.                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Physical death does not erase the target, nor does it free the slayer from cause and effect. It simply forces both into their next involuntary \"rise to become\" (*bhāva*) within *saṃsāra*. True freedom is not found in physical destruction, but in eradicating *rāga*, *dosa*, and *moha*, establishing Concentration (*Samādhi*) to pass through the pure abode Brahma realms as the gateway to exit this universe entirely into **Nibbāna-Dhātu**.                                          |


**2.[22](javascript:void(0))   vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya, navāni gṛhṇāti naro 'parāṇi;**

**        tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇāny, anyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī.**

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Just as a person discards worn-out garments and takes on other new ones, so the embodied (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman) discards worn-out physical bodies and enters into other new ones. |
+===================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[23](javascript:void(0))   nainaṁ chindanti śastrāṇi, nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ;**

**        na cainaṁ kledayanty āpo, na śoṣayati mārutaḥ.**

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Weapons do not cut this (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman), fire does not burn this; water does not wet this, nor does the wind dry this. |
+===============================================================================================================================+

**2.[24](javascript:void(0))   acchedyo 'yam adāhyo 'yam, akledyo 'śoṣya eva ca;**

**        nityaḥ sarva-gataḥ sthāṇur, acalo 'yaṁ sanātanaḥ.**

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| This (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman) cannot be cut, this cannot be burned, this cannot be wetted, nor dried indeed; continuously lasting (nitya), all-pervading (sarva-gata), stable (sthāṇu), immovable (acala), this is ancient (sanātana). |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **1). Structural Inviolability Across All Physical Elements**                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Following 2.23\'s description of active physical instruments (weapons, fire, water, wind), Kṛṣṇa now affirms the **inherent structural properties** of the embodied entity (*Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman*):                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Acchedya:** Inherent uncleavability---no blade can slice a non-material structure.                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Adāhya:** Inherent incombustibility---thermal energy cannot alter its higher-dimensional substance.                                                                                                                              |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Akledya & Aśoṣya:** Absolute resistance to moisture-induced decay and atmospheric desiccation.                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| 3D physical forces pass directly through it without making operational contact because it belongs to a higher-dimensional plane of reality.                                                                                          |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **2). Five Operational Qualities Related to Physical Elements**                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Nitya (Continuously Lasting):** Inwardly abiding (*ni-tya*), remaining fully continuous through every physical transition.                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Sarva-gata (All-pervading):** Not localized or bounded by a single physical world; it can inhabit, pervade, and transition across any world (*loka*) in the universe; because it is beyond physical.                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Sthāṇu (Stable):** Maintains its core integrity regardless of how chaotically the outer physical body (*asat*) breaks down.                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Acala (Immovable):** Unshaken by physical impact, gravitational pull, or material momentum.                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| - **Sanātana (Ancient):** existing from ancient times.                                                                                                                                                                               |
+======================================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[25](javascript:void(0))   avyakto 'yam acintyo 'yam, avikāryo 'yam ucyate;**

**        tasmād evaṁ viditvainaṁ, nānuśocitum arhasi.**

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| This (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman) is said to be unmanifest (avyakta), unapprehensible by ordinary discursive 3D thought (acintya), and immune to physical transformation (avikārya); therefore, knowing this to be such, you should not grieve. |
+===========================================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

**\**

**2.[26](javascript:void(0))   atha cainaṁ nitya-jātaṁ, nityaṁ vā manyase mṛtam;**

**        tathāpi tvaṁ mahā-bāho, nainaṁ śocitum arhasi.**

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Even if you think this (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman) is continuously born into physical being (nitya-jāta) or continuously undergoing physical death (nityam mṛtam), even then, O mighty-armed (Arjuna), you should not grieve over it. |
+==================================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[27](javascript:void(0))   jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyur, dhruvaṁ janma mṛtasya ca;**

**        tasmād aparihārye 'rthe, na tvaṁ śocitum arhasi.**

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| For to that which is born into physical existence, physical death is certain; and to that which undergoes physical death, physical birth is certain. Therefore, over an unavoidable matter, you should not grieve. |
+====================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[28](javascript:void(0))   avyaktādīni bhūtāni, vyakta-madhyāni bhārata;**

**        avyakta-nidhanāny eva, tatra kā paridevanā.**

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Unmanifest (avyakta) in their origin are living beings, manifest (vyakta) in their middle state, O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna), and unmanifest (avyakta) in their dissolution indeed---what room is there for lamentation in this? |
+=======================================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[29](javascript:void(0))   āścarya-vat paśyati kaścid enam, āścarya-vad vadati tathaiva cānyaḥ; āścarya-vac cainam anyaḥ śṛṇoti, śrutvāpy enaṁ veda na caiva kaścit.**

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Hardly anyone ever sees this (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman) as a marvel; hardly anyone speaks of it as a marvel; hardly anyone gets to hear of it as a marvel; and even after hearing, virtually no one at all directly discerns or penetrates it.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Commentary: The Four-Tiered Pyramid of Rarity**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Kṛṣṇa deliberately structures 2.29 as a progressive filter, illustrating how narrow the gateway to true spiritual realization of *Ātman* actually is inside this *saṃsāric world*:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Rarity of Direct Perception (*Paśyati Kaścit*):** Out of millions bound to 3D sensory contacts (*mātrā-sparśāḥ*), only an exceptionally rare individual breaks through sensory delusion to directly perceive the non-physical occupant (*Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman*).                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Rarity of Authentic Articulation (*Vadati Tathāiva Cānyaḥ*):** Even among those rare few who glimpse it, finding one who possesses the clarity to explain the unmanifest (*avyakta*), unalterable reality without falling back into physical metaphors is extraordinarily rare.                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Rarity of Hearing Authentic Dhamma (*Śṛṇoti Cānyaḥ*):** For a seeker inside *loka* to even come into contact with such a rare teacher and hear this true instruction represents an exceptionally rare alignment of prior *kammic* conditions.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **The Ultimate Bottleneck (*Śrutvāpy Enaṁ Veda Na Caiva Kaścit*):** Even when all three rare conditions are met---the teacher sees, the teacher speaks, and the student hears---the final step remains the hardest. Almost everyone stops at intellectual awe (*āścarya*), conceptual listening, or theoretical agreement. Directly penetrating (*veda*) and realizing this truth is the absolute rarest occurrence in the universe. |


**2.[30](javascript:void(0))   dehī nityam avadhyo 'yaṁ, dehe sarvasya bhārata;**

**        tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni, na tvaṁ śocitum arhasi.**

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| The embodied (Dehī, Śarīrin, Ātman) residing in the physical body of everyone is continuously indestructible (nityam avadhya) by physical means, O descendant of Bharata (Arjuna); therefore, over all living beings, you should not grieve. |
+==============================================================================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[31](javascript:void(0))   sva-dharmam api cāvekṣya, na vikampitum arhasi;**

**  dharmyād dhi yuddhāc chreyo 'nyat, kṣatriyasya na vidyate.**

+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Moreover, considering your own inherent duty (sva-dharma), you should not waver; for indeed, there exists no higher good for a warrior (kṣatriya) than a righteous war (dharmya yuddha). |
+==========================================================================================================================================================================================+

**2.[32](javascript:void(0))   yadṛcchayā copapannaṁ, svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam;**

**        sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha, labhante yuddham īdṛśam.**

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Unasked, presented by chance as a gateway to the noble heavenly realm of light (svarga-dvāram apāvṛtam)---fortunate indeed are the warriors (kṣatriyāḥ), O Pārtha (Arjuna), who obtain such a battle.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Commentary**: **The Unsought Gateway to Light**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| In this verse, Kṛṣṇa frames the impending battle not as an act of personal aggression or territorial conquest, but as an unsought opportunity (*yadṛcchayā upapannam*) that has arrived naturally:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| - **The Moral Duty of the Warrior (*Kṣatriya*):** For the descendants of Manu (mankind), society is maintained through distinct duties (*sva-dharma*). The specific duty of the warriors is the preservation of righteousness and the active protection of divine order against destructive forces (*adharma*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| - **The Open Door (*Apāvṛtam Dvāram*):** When a noble conflict is forced upon a warrior despite all peaceful efforts, engaging in it chivalrily becomes a noble act of protection. Dying in such a defense of the righteous acts as an immediate, transformative doorway (*svarga-dvāram*) that elevates the departing entity into *svarga*---the luminous, refined heavenly realms of light for Mankind.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **The Universal Archetype of the Noble Death**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Verse 2.32 aligns with ancient traditions: that laying down one\'s physical body (*śarīra*) in a chivalry act to protect the righteous generates immense wholesome *kammic* momentum. For mankind (*the descendants of Manu*), dying without personal malice or greed, purely out of duty, instantly cuts through low-level lower-realm attachments, drawing the embodied entity (*Dehī, Ātman*) into the radiant, higher-frequency planes of *svarga*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| When looking at the tradition of knighthood, chivalry, and the code of arms across human history, the notion of knightly virtue is rooted in a universal archetype: the warrior whose physical strength is bound, governed, and ennobled by moral duty, self-discipline, and protection of the divine order (Brahmavihara). For reference let's examine the medieval codes like the *Song of Roland* and the Arthurian codes---reveal **9 Core Virtues** that defined the true ancient knight.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **(1). Prowess (*Prouesse* / Courage in Action)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Prowess was not merely skill with a blade or lance; it was the active, physical execution of courage. A knight was expected to cultivate bodily strength, martial mastery, and unwavering valor under life-or-death pressure. Without physical prowess, a knight could not defend the weak; without virtue, prowess was merely brutality.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **(2). Justice (*Justice* / Uprightness)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| A knight was sworn to defend the right, the just, and the lawful cause above personal gain. Justice meant standing as a bulwark against tyranny, exploitation, and chaos. It demanded that power be exercised with absolute fairness, regardless of whether dealing with a peer, a king, or a humble peasant.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **(3). Loyalty (*Loyauté* / Fealty)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
